nodes.claim: A typed claims graph with a criteria-governed evidence ladder is a well-precedented substrate for machine-written theory — the structure is inherited from real prior art; the benefit is a bet this program must measure, not cite.
nodes.detail: Raised argued→cited 2026-08-26 with the claim narrowed to what the evidence licenses; go-9 carries the counter-evidence that forced the narrowing (its edge landed as refines rather than contradicts precisely because this claim conceded the point — go-6 has the typing rule). Structural precedent, each element separately: typed deliberation nodes — IBIS (Kunz & Rittel 1970: topics, issues, questions of fact, positions, arguments and model problems as element types; built for coordinating contested planning, with no evidence ladder and 'settling' as a social act) and gIBIS at tool scale (Conklin & Begeman 1988, typed IBIS networks over a shared database). Contradictions as first-class structure — Dung 1995 makes attack a first-class relation from which acceptance is computable, the formal license for the contradicts edge; SWAN (Ciccarese et al. 2008) was designed to foreground contradictory assertions in community discourse. The closest built precedent is micropublications (Clark, Ciccarese & Goble 2014): claims as nodes, supports and challenges as typed edges, and structural health queries — the model's competency questions include listing assertions unsupported by evidence (body-level content, index-grade; paraphrase, not quotation) — which is this lane's orphan/health practice a decade early; ORKG (Jaradeh et al. 2019) is the at-scale existence proof. The ladder's precedent is GRADE (Guyatt et al. 2008): four ordered levels of evidence quality (the 2008 paper's own term; 'certainty' is later GRADE wording) whose movement is governed by NAMED criteria — the import being that a ladder without named transition criteria is not GRADE-like, which is why §4 defines each rung by the evidence it requires and why go-8's per-source grades matter. One consequence recorded from Dung rather than smoothed over: there, status is DERIVED from the attack graph under a semantics; here it is stamped per node with named criteria. The reconciliation this program runs: the stamped ladder is the GRADE half, and the health instrument's contradiction count (go-5) is the Dung half's seed — a node under an unresolved contradicts edge is challenged regardless of its stamped rung. What remains uncitable is efficacy: the argumentation literature the design-rationale field imported its usefulness claims from had, by 1994, failed to substantiate them (go-9). Progress-as-status-motion stays this program's own wager, measured by its own health numbers.

nodes.claim: Accumulating knowledge bases decay measurably; this program measures its graphs on the literature's own health dimensions and treats pruning as first-class — transferring that discipline to machine-written theory graphs is its own, still-unmeasured bet.
nodes.detail: Raised argued→cited 2026-08-26 with the claim restated to what the sources reach: they ground the dimensions and the decay, not a diagnosis of THIS program — no cited corpus is a machine-written claims graph, so the transfer clause is load-bearing, exactly as in go-1. The dimension mapping: staleness→timeliness, near-duplicates→conciseness, contradictions→consistency, orphans→interlinking, four of the 18 quality dimensions (69 metrics) the linked-data quality survey systematized (Zaveri et al. 2016); and 'refinement' — completion PLUS error detection — is half of a named research area, so pruning is first-class in the literature too, not just in this charter (Paulheim 2017). The decay evidence, cross-domain: in Stack Overflow, 58.4% of obsolete answers were probably obsolete when first posted and only 20.5% are ever updated once observed obsolete (Zhang et al. 2021) — rot is often BORN, not aged, so go-5's timestamp-based staleness metric is a lower bound, same epistemic shape as go-6's contradiction count; one in five STM articles (1997–2012 corpus) suffers reference rot, and the companion study found three of four URI references lead to content that has drifted (Klein et al. 2014; Jones et al. 2016) — a cited node's health decays through its links while its text never changes, which is the charter's §11 source-rot rule and go-8's verification-grade labels stated as measured fact; and in maintained software documentation, up-to-dateness and completeness issues are both frequently mentioned in a mined taxonomy of 878 artifacts (Aghajani et al. 2019) — decay and gaps co-dominate; the abstract names no single dominant failure. One caution absorbed from the strongest counter-result: Wikipedia's quality-control tooling measurably crippled the growth it was built to manage (Halfaker et al. 2013) — pruning policy is a system variable with second-order costs, which is why go-5 keeps every metric descriptive and every prune a judged act with a log row, never a gate.
sources: Zaveri A, Rula A, Maurino A, Pietrobon R, Lehmann J, Auer S 2016, 'Quality assessment for Linked Data: A Survey', Semantic Web 7(1):63-93, DOI 10.3233/SW-150175 (online-first 2015; cited by issue). Index-grade; dimension NAMES corroborated multi-index, their grouping into categories deliberately not quoted

nodes.claim: Cross-graph structure is where the combination lives, so global ids and typed cross-edges are load-bearing, not decoration.
nodes.detail: Central's combination theory is largely MADE of cross-graph edges (gen-3 supports cen-1, pat-4 supports cen-2). The optimizer therefore validates cross-references every run (no dangling ids), keeps id prefixes stable forever, and treats a broken cross-edge as a build failure, not a cosmetic one.

nodes.claim: Self-optimization is legitimate exactly when it is versioned, total and reversible.
nodes.detail: This lane may change the schema and its own methods — the owner asked for a graph optimizer 'including itself' — under three bounds: every schema change bumps the version and migrates ALL graphs in the same run or does not land; changes are reversible from git history; and the optimizer never rewrites another lane's CONTENT (claims, statuses, details) — only structure (format, merges of literal duplicates with a log row, id hygiene). Content is each lane's; shape is this lane's.

nodes.claim: Graph health is a committed measurement instrument — named metrics with named thresholds, computed by a tool in the repo — never a hand count in a summary.
nodes.detail: The first scheduled run replaced hand-counting with graph/health.mjs: per lane, status mix, stale conjectures (untouched >14 days), orphans (program-wide degree zero; the rate is the list over the node count) and detail weight (>400 words flagged); program-wide, unresolved contradicts edges and near-duplicate claim pairs (token Jaccard ≥ 0.5, cross-graph pairs included). Three design choices carry the theory. (a) Thresholds are named constants in the tool, so changing one is a reviewable diff rather than drift in a summary's prose. (b) Orphan degree is program-wide: a node referenced only from another lane's graph is not an orphan, because cross-graph edges are the combination (go-3) — a per-file orphan count would misread exactly the nodes central most depends on. (c) The tool is descriptive, never gating: check.mjs holds form, health.mjs reports signals, and the judgment (merge, prune, flag, ignore) stays with the optimizer — every metric here is a proxy a lane could Goodhart the moment it gates (trivial edges to dodge the orphan count, detail sharded into filler nodes to dodge the budget). Near-duplicate flags in particular are candidates to READ, not to merge: token overlap cannot tell a duplicate from a deliberate cross-lane mirror (bod-2/gen-2), and only literal duplicates are ever merged (§5). First measurement, 2026-08-26: 43 nodes, 59 edges (25 cross-graph), mix 12 conjecture / 22 argued / 9 cited / 0 measured, zero contradictions recorded, zero near-duplicate pairs at threshold, six nodes over detail budget. Interpretation caveat, added the same day from go-2's evidence: the staleness metric is a timestamp proxy and rot is often born rather than aged (Zhang et al. 2021, at go-2), so a low stale count is a lower bound on decay, not an all-clear. 2026-08-28: the instrument gains a per-lane graded-sources count — source-string verification markers only ('-grade' suffix in the sources array), the one placement countable without interpreting prose; grades written into detail prose are deliberately not counted, because the suffix is now homonymous between verification labels and domain adjectives and only a reader can tell them apart (go-10 has the evidence). The metric exists to price what an eventual schema-defined grade field would inherit, not to push adoption of a convention go-10 records as non-propagating. 2026-09-01: the instrument gains run recency — each lane's last LOG.md row date and age, silence flagged past SILENT_DAYS=2 (go-11 carries the argument and the limits).

nodes.claim: A zero in the contradiction metric measures recording, not harmony: adversarial findings that die in prose leave the graph looking more agreed than the program is.
nodes.detail: Measured fact, first health pass (2026-08-26): zero contradicts edges across 43 nodes — after three scout runs whose adversarial passes each forced substantive corrections. Within-run corrections rightly vanish into the rewritten claim; the gap is standing, surviving tension: the one genuine cross-lane tension then live (gen-5's LLM analogy against pat-6's cited negative results) was typed refines, indistinguishable from a friendly sharpening, and the count read 0. Consequence for the instrument (go-5): the contradiction count is a lower bound on live disagreement — a tension registers only when some lane elects the strongest edge type. Practice offered, not imposed (content is the lanes', §5): when external evidence cuts against a claim another node STILL asserts, type contradicts and let the target resolve it into a refinement; once the target has narrowed, refines is the honest type (go-9→go-1 is the worked example — it landed refines because go-1 absorbed the critique the same run). A contradicts edge is a work item a later run is forced to see. Exercised end-to-end 2026-08-27→29, with no optimizer involvement: tests elected the program's first contradicts edge in exactly the offered split-verdict shape (tst-6→cen-1, contradicts scoped to the singular cen-1 still asserted, refines for the half it sharpened); central's next run revised cen-1 to the hierarchical fork, naming the edge as what it resolved; the electing lane then retired the contradicts with full accounting after a clause-by-clause re-read — refines kept, supports added as a third option beyond the two central offered — and recorded the residual tension at tst-5/tst-8 instead. Two days, election to resolution. New count semantics from that cycle: a reading of 0 is now ambiguous between never-elected and elected-and-resolved; the point-in-time instrument cannot distinguish them (resolution traces live in LOG rows and the nodes' own accounting), so the health summary narrates resolutions rather than reading 0 as concord — and go-11 generalizes the same blindness: content metrics also read clean when the program has simply stopped recording. The lower-bound caveat stands on every reading.

nodes.claim: Detail has a weight budget: past a few hundred words a node is an essay wearing one status, and the fix is fission into nodes the ladder can grip separately.
nodes.detail: First measurement (2026-08-26): six of 43 nodes over the 400-word budget, all born cited from scout runs; three of the six hand-labeled sub-claims inline to keep rungs separate (strings verified then) — lanes doing manually what node granularity does structurally. One-node-one-status only checks anything while a node carries roughly one claim (go-1): a 700-word detail hides which sentence the status covers and hands the skeptic no target smaller than the whole essay. Fission restores per-claim status at zero information cost. Boundary honored: splitting content is the owning lane's act; the optimizer flags weight (health.mjs) and records the pattern here. A smell threshold, not a gate (go-5's Goodhart argument). Second measurement (2026-08-28): 23 of 69 over budget — 33%, from 14% two days earlier (11% on the same-day nine-graph state; either baseline, the jump is real) — the maximum more than doubled (map-6 1531w), argument-only nodes crossing too, zero fissions; verdict then: the flag as published changes no behavior, because no flagged lane's read path surfaces it, and the lever chosen was central — the one lane that reads everything and may append to every QUESTIONS.md. Third measurement (2026-09-01): the lever worked — three parents fissioned within two days of central routing the measurement by name: cen-2→cen-8 (central's own same-run read of this graph), gen-5→gen-12/gen-13 (central's 08-28 QUESTIONS append, adopted next run 'per central'), tst-5→tst-8 (tests' own adversarial pass forced it under tests' cited-string precedent, the fission also answering central's placement question) — go-10 has the channel accounting. Yet the rate ROSE: 29 of 80 over budget (36%), because scout runs keep landing heavy nodes and fission children themselves cross the budget (gen-12 710w, gen-13 486w; tst-5 still 789w after fission). Mid-land, the last two flagged offenders confirmed the verdict: map and pattern's 09-01 catch-up runs (landed 13:11, during this run's own land step) fissioned exactly the nodes central named — map-6 1531→705w with an honest cited→argued demotion, pat-3 899→528w — the fourth and fifth fissions, and BOTH parents plus two new children (map-7 431w, map-8 575w) remain over budget, so the post-fission rate is 31 of 88 (35%): fission barely moves it, because fission conserves words. Verdict: fission restores statuses the ladder can grip, but it does not by itself pay the budget — the budget binds at write time or not at all, an authoring discipline the in-lane adversarial pass alone has independently enforced (tst-5).

nodes.claim: The lanes run a finer evidence scale than the schema knows — per-source verification grades — and if the schema ever absorbs it, it will be as a defined vocabulary: waiting for the emergent convention to settle was measured to be waiting on something the architecture cannot produce.
nodes.detail: Bottom-up observation, three scout runs in: genetic, map and pattern each independently invented per-source verification grading, in three different vocabularies — genetic writes 'abstract-grade' and 'vendor-grade' inline; pattern writes 'abstract/snippet/repo-table-grade' and 'index-grade'; map writes per-node 'Verification grade:' sentences ('full text', 'abstract level') with no suffix convention — and map and genetic additionally mark own-inference sub-claims inline (go-7 has the strings). Same instinct three ways is schema pressure: cited is one rung, but what the lanes actually record is which source cleared which bar, and today that lives in strings where check.mjs cannot hold it (a 'full text' label can silently outlive the verification it names, and nothing forces a grade at all). Candidate schema v2: an optional enumerated grade per source entry, checkable and countable by health.mjs. Why not this run: the vocabulary is one day old and still moving — three lanes, three overlapping but different label sets — and a schema change migrates every graph in the same run or does not land (§5, go-4); that migration is cheap at 43 nodes and grows with the corpus, but an enum frozen too early forces a v3 when the convention settles differently, which doubles exactly the cost the rule exists to bound. Decision rule: revisit after the three unscouted lanes (body, questions, tests) have each run a scout — if the grade vocabulary holds across six lanes it is stable enough to freeze, and the cost curve then says migrate promptly rather than let string-grade sources accumulate. THE RULE FIRED 2026-08-28: all three lanes have scouted, and the vocabulary did not hold — it proliferated and split (census and verdict at go-10, which now carries the decision). No v2 grade enum lands, and the original claim's 'once the convention stops moving' clause is retired as wrong-headed rather than merely premature: the convention was never going to stop moving on its own, because nothing carries one lane's style to another (go-10's mechanism). What survives of this node: the observation that lanes independently want per-source grading was real and still stands — three MORE vocabularies appeared after it was written — and the cost-curve argument (unstructured grade strings accumulate migration debt) transfers intact to go-10's schema-defined path.

nodes.claim: The efficacy of argumentation substrates is unproven, not proven: the argumentation literature design rationale imported its usefulness claims from had failed to substantiate them, and — by this lane's own inference — two of the four documented formalization costs survive a machine author.
nodes.detail: This node exists to keep go-1 honest. The evidence, stated with its own limits. (1) Buckingham Shum & Hammond 1994 examined the two foundational claims of argumentation-based design rationale — that expressing rationale as argumentation is useful, and that designers can use the notations — and found that research into semiformal argumentation OUTSIDE the design context had 'failed to substantiate convincingly either' (their scope qualifier, kept: the imported literature failed to license the claims, which is not the same as the field disconfirming itself); the same abstract also reports emerging indications that argumentation-based rationale CAN assist certain kinds of design reasoning and be useful later — this is a mixed source, cited as one. The sting stands: the same first author later built ScholOnto, a claim-centric scholarly graph (Buckingham Shum et al. 2000) — builder and doubter are one person, the posture this program should copy. (2) Of the four named problems of formal representation (Shipman & Marshall 1999) — cognitive overhead, tacit knowledge, premature structure, situational structure — this lane's own inference, marked as such: the first two largely dissolve for a machine author, which pays the discretization cost without reluctance or interruption, while premature structure and situational structure do not — forcing a nascent idea into claim-plus-status before the right decomposition is known is go-7's essay-node pathology from the other side, and a fixed type/status vocabulary fits some theory domains worse than others. Their prescription, incremental formalization, is partially absorbed by the conjecture rung and go-8's rule against freezing a moving convention. (3) gIBIS's own authors reported the 'rather austere selection of node and link types' made discretizing vague thought unnatural (Conklin & Begeman 1988, snippet-grade). Edge typing, per go-6's own rule: this landed as refines, not contradicts, because go-1 narrowed its claim to concede exactly this point in the same run — had go-1 kept its unconditional 'right substrate' form, this would be the program's first contradicts edge. The open question it leaves is empirical: months of real status motion without padding substantiates the bet locally; stagnation-by-rewording means the critique won, and the digest is where that verdict becomes visible.
sources: Buckingham Shum S, Hammond N 1994, 'Argumentation-based design rationale: what use at what cost?', International Journal of Human-Computer Studies 40(4):603-652, DOI 10.1006/ijhc.1994.1029. Index-grade, conclusion abstract-grade

Shipman FM III, Marshall CC 1999, 'Formality Considered Harmful: Experiences, Emerging Themes, and Directions on the Use of Formal Representations in Interactive Systems', Computer Supported Cooperative Work 8(4):333-352, DOI 10.1023/A:1008716330212. Index-grade, four-problem taxonomy abstract-grade

Conklin J, Begeman ML 1988, 'gIBIS: a hypertext tool for exploratory policy discussion', ACM TOIS/TOOIS 6(4):303-331, DOI 10.1145/58566.59297 — cost quotes snippet-grade from a hosted PDF, wording unconfirmed at source

Buckingham Shum S, Motta E, Domingue J 2000, 'ScholOnto: an ontology-based digital library server for research documents and discourse', International Journal on Digital Libraries 3(3):237-248, DOI 10.1007/s007990000034. Index-grade

nodes.claim: Unschematized conventions do not converge across fresh-session lanes — they proliferate and drift into homonymy; convergence happens only through an active channel (an enforced artifact, central's read-path relay, or in-lane adversarial re-derivation), so schema absorption is an act of coordination, never a ratification of emergence.
nodes.detail: Measured 2026-08-28, two days after go-8. Census over all nine graphs (recomputable from the tree): 18 distinct '-grade' tokens — 16 excluding this lane's own meta-prose — from 11 by the same census when go-8 was written. The suffix is homonymous — 'record-grade' states how a source was verified; tests' 'instrument-grade model' is a domain adjective (contexts re-verified 2026-09-01; the census's other adjective instance, central's 'instrument-grade standard', was deleted in cen-1's 08-28 revision — inline grade strings rot as go-2 predicts). Placement split four ways: two source-string syntaxes (this lane and database; genetic — a co-inventor — in a third syntax at only 5/98), pattern in detail prose with zero source markers, map in free-form sentences; newly scouted lanes adopted none. Mechanism, this lane's own inference: a run is a fresh session reading the charter, the schema and its own files, so propagation follows the RECEIVING lane's read path — 'instrument-grade' crossed lanes via central's append to tests' QUESTIONS.md, a file tests is chartered to read, while genetic's graded source strings propagated nowhere. Read-path carriage moves tokens, not conventions (tests absorbed the homonymous adjective, not the grading practice). Confirmed 2026-09-01 across eight further observations, every one obeying a read path: central — chartered to read all graphs — absorbed go-7 directly and fissioned cen-2 the same run; its QUESTIONS appends carried fission to genetic, a pricing ask to questions and the go-6-shaped retype ask to tests, and all three lanes adopted on their next run; the same appends to map and pattern moved nothing for four days simply because those lanes did not run — then both adopted in their 09-01 catch-up runs (landed 13:11, during this run's land step), relay complete at 5-for-5 — a read path propagates exactly when the reader runs; and tests' tst-5 fission arrived through no cross-lane carriage at all — its own adversarial pass re-derived the discipline from an in-lane precedent, a convergence generator independent of read paths. Consequence: convergence needs an active channel — enforced artifacts (schema plus checker), central's QUESTIONS relay, or in-lane adversarial re-derivation; passive availability moves nothing. Standing verdicts: go-8's rule fired, answer no — emergence was the wrong test; any future grade field is schema-defined, lane-populated, optional-and-empty at migration (the migrate-all-in-one-run rule bounds mechanical migration to what a script derives without reading); optionality enforces vocabulary, not adoption; health.mjs counts source-string markers only, pricing what such a field would inherit.

nodes.claim: Run cadence is a graph-health dimension no content metric can see: every prior signal is a function of what the graphs say, so a program that stops running reads as maximally healthy — each lane's run recency must be measured alongside content.
nodes.detail: Measured 2026-09-01: zero landings program-wide from 2026-08-29 (four odd-date lanes) until this run — the even-date group (database, map, pattern, graph-optimizer, central) missed its 08-30 cycle entirely, the odd-date group (genetic, body, questions, tests) missed 08-31 — and the odd-date group's 09-01 slots (09:02–12:02 UTC) had passed landing nothing by this run's write (~13:00 UTC) — and the weekly digest, due on central's first firing after Sunday 08-30 00:00 UTC (§6), is unwritten — DIGEST.md still reads 2026-08-26. This run itself fired on 09-01, off this lane's even-date schedule — consistent with recovery or manual dispatch; the cause is not observable from the tree. Nor from the account side, checked this run: all nine Routines read enabled with no run-outcome record — dispatcher-bound Routines record none by contract, so those absences are uninformative (the dispatcher session's transcript, owner-readable per §10, is the one record outside the tree) — so among the artifacts any lane or the digest reads, silence shows only in the branch, and only if measured. Every pre-existing signal (status mix, staleness, orphans, contradictions, duplicates, detail weight) is computed from graph content, constant under a stopped program; the 08-30/08-31 gap sat under a green checker and a clean health report until this run compared dates by hand. This is go-6's blindness generalized — silence is the recording rate at zero — and it inverts go-2's decay lens: a silent corpus neither rots visibly nor lives. Remedy, same run: health.mjs reports each lane's last LOG.md row date and age, flagging silence past SILENT_DAYS=2 — LOG.md is the signal because it is append-only, one row per run, and a nothing-advanced run still logs (§3), where graph.updated moves only on content — and the flag lands in the digest-facing summary, re-pacing staying the owner's dial (§11); descriptive, never gating (go-5). Limits, named: the metric trusts each row's leading date; a lane padding rows would read alive (§3's ratchet names that failure); and the flag's availability depends on some lane running — a measurement that vanishes with the program it measures, which is why the silence row belongs in every run's summary. Concrete cost: map's and pattern's routed fission questions (go-7) sat unread the whole gap, then were acted on in recovery's first hour — both landed off-schedule catch-ups at 13:11, during this run's land step, the odd group's slots still unfilled; six of nine lanes flag silent at close.
